items.title: Diesel Prices Keep Pressure on Fed and Markets
items.content: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers confront inflation that remains above target and uncertainty tied to geopolitical developments. Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Mozambique Cut by Moody’s on Heightened Restructuring Risks
items.content: Moody’s Ratings cut its assessment of Mozambique’s creditworthiness deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond.

summaries.en: Moody’s downgraded Mozambique’s credit rating further into junk status due to heightened risks of the country restructuring its sole eurobond. The rating agency cited concerns about the gas-rich southeast African nation’s financial stability. The move reflects Moody’s assessment of increased likelihood of debt restructuring, impacting Mozambique’s creditworthiness.

items.title: US Greenland Deal Shifts Focus to Investment
items.content: A new security agreement between the US, Denmark and Greenland would expand the American military role while preserving Greenlandic sovereignty, shifting attention toward potential US investment in mining, infrastructure and tourism. Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that Greenland welcomes investment but faces formidable obstacles including limited transportation infrastructure, a small workforce and the high cost of developing projects in the Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens highlighted these obstacles during a Bloomberg interview. (Word count: 50)

items.title: UN Talks Offer a New Opening on Iran War
items.content: World leaders head to the UN General Assembly as Gulf states seek renewed diplomacy to reduce attacks, restore more predictable energy flows and move the Iran war away from active conflict. Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and other regional infrastructure are adding urgency to those efforts as Gulf economies face mounting pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 联合国大会召开之际，海湾国家寻求通过外交手段减少冲突、恢复能源供应稳定，推动伊朗战事降温。布鲁金斯学会的苏珊娜·马尔尼表示，沙特东西向管道等区域基础设施的动荡加剧了海湾国家面临的压力，促使各方加快外交努力。此举旨在缓解紧张局势，促进地区稳定。（来源：彭博社）
summaries.en: World leaders are attending the UN General Assembly as Gulf states push for renewed diplomacy with Iran to reduce attacks, restore stable energy flows, and de-escalate the conflict. Disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and regional infrastructure are increasing urgency, as Gulf economies face pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Trump Moves to Bar Three News Outlets From White House
items.content: President Donald Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over coverage he calls “fake news,” though questions remain about how the restrictions would be enforced and whether they could face legal challenges. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses how this move comes as Trump also faces protests over the future of the Kennedy Center and prepares to address the UN General Assembly with the Iran war expected to be a major focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Buffett Son Takes Chair as Berkshire Transition Ends
items.content: Warren Buffett has stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after more than six decades at the company, becoming chairman emeritus as his son Howard takes over the board and Greg Abel remains CEO. Bloomberg News Insurance Reporter Alex Rajbhandari explains that Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director since 1993, is tasked with safeguarding the company’s culture and values as the conglomerate completes its long-planned leadership transition. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: AI Agents Test the Limits of Human Oversight
items.content: OpenAI disclosed six cases of unexpected or concerning model behavior as AI companies grapple with how to monitor increasingly autonomous agents and whether stronger independent oversight is needed. Joining David Gura on Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Shirin Ghaffary explains that the safety debate is taking on geopolitical urgency as President Donald Trump emphasizes maintaining the US lead over China while resisting calls to slow AI development. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: JPMorgan Sees No Clear Endgame for Oil Markets
items.content: An attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline has disrupted a crucial route around the Strait of Hormuz, threatening crude deliveries to Europe and adding pressure to already tight diesel markets. On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy discusses how JPMorgan says it no longer has a baseline view for oil markets as the Iran conflict, attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and uncertainty over Chinese demand make the outlook increasingly difficult to model. (Source: Bloomberg)

The attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline threatens crude deliveries to Europe and exacerbates tight diesel markets.

items.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
items.content: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth.  (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 黑石集团首席运营官格雷认为，印度年轻人口、壮大中产阶级和改善的基础设施正吸引全球投资者。但年轻人口优势也带来压力：每年有数百万年轻人毕业，而正规就业岗位增长未能满足其技能和期望。同时，各邦正通过削减监管、建设工业基础设施等方式争夺投资，涵盖电子、半导体等领域。印度能否将规模、人才和投资势头转化为足够的生产性就业，以支撑其增长，仍是关键问题。
summaries.en: India's young population and expanding middle class, along with improving infrastructure, are attracting global investors, as noted by Blackstone COO Jon Gray. However, millions of young graduates face a mismatch between their skills and available jobs, as formal-sector job creation lags. States are competing for investment by easing regulations and targeting sectors like electronics and semiconductors. The key challenge is whether India can convert its demographic and investment potential into sustainable, productive growth.

items.title: World Running Short of Supertankers Threatens Long-Haul Oil Flow
items.content: The soaring cost of moving oil around the world is making some long-distance crude trades uneconomical, threatening to disrupt flows at a time when fuel markets have never been tighter.

summaries.en: Rising shipping costs are rendering some long-distance oil trades unprofitable, potentially disrupting global crude flows amid tight fuel markets. The scarcity of supertankers exacerbates the issue, threatening the viability of long-haul oil transportation.

summaries.en: Bolivia's government abolished its diesel subsidy following Senate approval of a $1.9 billion IMF loan, which requires spending restrictions. The move aligns with the IMF's conditions for financial assistance.

items.title: Blackstone Sees India Nearing Tipping Point for Foreign Capital
items.content: As Jon Gray recalls it, Blackstone Inc.’s first foray into India started slowly and then ran into headwinds during the global financial crisis.

summaries.en: Blackstone Inc. began its operations in India with gradual progress but faced challenges during the global financial crisis. The article suggests India may be approaching a critical juncture for foreign capital inflows.

items.title: China’s Fiscal Pullback Extends to August as Spending Slumps
items.content: China’s public expenditure declined at a quicker rate in August, indicating the government was still withdrawing fiscal support for the economy despite cooling growth momentum.
items.contentSnippet: China’s public expenditure declined at a quicker rate in August, indicating the government was still withdrawing fiscal support for the economy despite cooling growth momentum.
items.creator: Bloomberg News

summaries.zh: 中国8月份公共支出下降速度加快，显示政府仍在撤出财政支持，尽管经济增长动能有所放缓。
summaries.en: China's public expenditure fell more sharply in August, signaling continued government fiscal withdrawal amid slowing economic growth. The data suggests the government is maintaining its policy of reducing fiscal support, even as growth momentum cools.

items.title: South Korea’s Justice Minister Nominee Withdraws After Reshuffle
items.content: South Korea’s nominee for justice minister has withdrawn from consideration for the role before being confirmed, the second ministerial nominee to pull out in a week after the president reshuffled his cabinet.
items.contentSnippet: South Korea’s nominee for justice minister has withdrawn from consideration for the role before being confirmed, the second ministerial nominee to pull out in a week after the president reshuffled his cabinet.
items.creator: Youkyung Lee

summaries.zh: 韩国总统改组内阁后，司法部长提名人选在确认前退出考虑，这是本周第二位撤回的部长提名人。
summaries.en: South Korea's nominee for justice minister withdrew from consideration before confirmation, following the president's cabinet reshuffle. This marks the second ministerial nominee to withdraw in a week. The withdrawal occurred prior to the official confirmation process.

items.title: Mark Walter’s Lieutenants Give Prosecutors Firsthand Accounts
items.content: Federal prosecutors have collected statements from some of billionaire Mark Walter’s most senior executives as authorities probe dealings at his insurance companies and the investment firm he runs, Guggenheim Partners LLC, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
items.contentSnippet: Federal prosecutors have collected statements from some of billionaire Mark Walter’s most senior executives as authorities probe dealings at his insurance companies and the investment firm he runs, Guggenheim Partners LLC, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
items.creator: Zachary R. Mider, Ava Benny-Morrison and Loukia Gyftopoulou

summaries.zh: 联邦检方已从亿万富翁马克·沃特（Mark Walter）的部分高级管理人员处收集了证词，以调查其保险公司及旗下投资公司Guggenheim Partners LLC的涉事交易。此事目前正由当局展开调查。
summaries.en: Federal prosecutors are investigating Mark Walter’s insurance companies and Guggenheim Partners LLC. They have gathered firsthand accounts from some of Walter’s top executives as part of the probe. The executives provided statements to the prosecutors, offering insights into the company’s operations and dealings under Walter’s leadership. The investigation is part of a broader examination into the business practices and financial activities of Walter’s firms.

items.title: Wall Street Week | India’s Growth Test, Bangalore’s Infrastructure Problem, Cricket Attracts Capital
items.content: This week, a special edition of Wall Street Week from the fastest growing large economy in the world: India. The country's technology sector has helped power its growth, but its success has led to uneven progress that could turn its strengths into weaknesses. Bangalore became India’s tech capital by attracting global investment and growing a deep talent pool, but infrastructure and policies to support the expansion have struggled to keep up. Plus, can Hyderabad overtake Bangalore as India’s leading tech city? Later, Blackstone’s investment in Royal Challengers Bengaluru reflects just how much potential India’s sports and entertainment economy has.  (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 《华尔街周报》聚焦增长中的印度。该国科技业推动经济高速发展，但区域发展不均。班加罗尔作为印度科技中心，吸引全球投资和人才，但基础设施和政策滞后。黑石投资皇家挑战者班加罗尔队，凸显印度体育娱乐经济的潜力。印度科技扩张面临挑战，其他城市如海得拉巴或成新增长点。
summaries.en: India's rapid growth, driven by its tech sector, faces challenges due to uneven progress. Bangalore, a global tech hub, struggles with inadequate infrastructure and policies, while Hyderabad may challenge its dominance. Blackstone's investment in Royal Challengers Bengaluru highlights India's potential in sports and entertainment. (50 words)
